}

/* the comment menu's trigger takes the padding so all of it is clickable */

  margin-bottom: 10px;

# TypeScript sketches (c1)

`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`: **no behaviour change.** Placement and pointing are
attributes read only by CSS, so the class gains no fields, no observedAttributes, no measuring.
Only the header comment grows by one line:

```ts
// A menu button following https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/ with no Fomantic.
// Markup: <aria-menu><button type="button">label</button><div class="menu"><a class="item">...</a></div></aria-menu>
// Optional host attributes, CSS only: placement="bottom-end|top-start|top-end" (default bottom-start), pointing
// Items get real focus (roving tabindex) instead of aria-activedescendant, see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md
```

The attribute vocabulary as a type, for the reader only (not added to the codebase, nothing consumes it):

```ts
type AriaMenuPlacement = 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'top-start' | 'top-end';
type AriaMenuHostAttrs = {placement?: AriaMenuPlacement; pointing?: ''};
```

## web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts — createTippy's onShow wrapper

The tooltip moves from the roleless host to the trigger (so `attachLazyTooltip`'s aria-label lands on
an element AT reads). Two facts then bite: tippy's `onShow` overwrites `aria-controls` (which
`<aria-menu>` set to the popup id), and the tooltip can show over the open menu on re-hover. One guard
fixes both, keyed on attributes `<aria-menu>` already sets. tippy's own menus set
`aria-haspopup="true"`, so they are unaffected.

```ts
onShow: (instance: Instance) => {
  const isMenuButton = target.getAttribute('aria-haspopup') === 'menu'; // an <aria-menu> trigger
  if (isMenuButton && target.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') return false; // don't cover the open menu
  // hide other tooltip instances so only one tooltip shows at a time
  for (const visibleInstance of visibleInstances) { /* unchanged */ }
  visibleInstances.add(instance);
  if (!isMenuButton) target.setAttribute('aria-controls', instance.popper.id); // keep pointing at the menu
  return onShow?.(instance);
},
```

Why no explicit hide on open: mouse open = click, and tooltips use `hideOnClick: true`; keyboard
open moves focus into the menu, and tippy's `focus` trigger hides on blur. The guard covers the rest
(pointer re-entering the trigger while open). Replaces what `common-page.ts` did for `jump` hosts.

## web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts — showTemporaryTooltip (:190)

```ts
target = target.closest('.ui.dropdown, aria-menu') ?? target; // the picked item is hidden by now
```

## web_src/js/features/common-page.ts — initFooterLanguageMenu (:27)

```ts
document.querySelector('.page-footer .menu.language-menu')?.addEventListener('click', async (e) => {
```

Keyboard picks reach this handler because `<aria-menu>` calls `item.click()` on Enter/Space.

- `dropdown.ts`, `common-page.ts` `initGlobalDropdown` (the hosts simply stop matching `.ui.dropdown`).

// AC7 sketch: tests/e2e/navbar-menus.test.ts (profile) and an added test in tests/e2e/issue-comment.test.ts (comment "...").
// Both drive the real page by keyboard only, assert one behaviour per regression we can name, and stay under ~2s each.
import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {login, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateIssue, randomString, assertNoJsError} from './utils.ts';

// regressions caught: trigger lost its name (tooltip left on the roleless host), menu opened off-screen
// (placement lost), item keyboard pick doesn't navigate, Escape doesn't restore focus
test('profile menu is operable by keyboard', async ({page}) => {
  await login(page);
  await page.goto('/');
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Profile and Settings…'});
  const menu = page.getByRole('menu');

  await trigger.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Profile'})).toBeFocused();

  // right-aligned under the trigger, so it stays inside the viewport
  const [menuBox, viewport] = [(await menu.boundingBox())!, page.viewportSize()!];
  expect(menuBox.x + menuBox.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(viewport.width);

  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Sign Out'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await page.keyboard.press('s'); // Starred
  await page.keyboard.press('s'); // Subscriptions
  await page.keyboard.press('s'); // Settings
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/user\/settings$/);
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

// regressions caught: kebab unnamed, a non-link item ignores Enter, Copy feedback tooltip lands at 0,0
// (showTemporaryTooltip still looking for .ui.dropdown)
test('comment menu is operable by keyboard', async ({page, request}) => {
  const repoName = `e2e-comment-menu-${randomString(8)}`;
  const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName, autoInit: false});
  await Promise.all([
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo: repoName, title: 'Comment menu test'}),
    login(page),
  ]);
  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}/issues/1`);
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'More Operations'}).first();

  await trigger.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Copy Link'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  // "Copied!" or "Copy failed" depending on the browser's clipboard permission; either way it must sit by the trigger
  const tooltip = page.getByRole('tooltip');
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();
  const [tipBox, triggerBox] = [(await tooltip.boundingBox())!, (await trigger.boundingBox())!];
  expect(Math.abs(tipBox.y - triggerBox.y)).toBeLessThan(80);
  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await page.keyboard.press('e'); // Edit
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Cancel'})).toBeVisible(); // the inline editor opened
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

# #62 candidate c1: declarative placement, zero component JS

Sketch files: `sketch/templates.md`, `sketch/css.md`, `sketch/ts.md`, `sketch/navbar-menus.test.ts`.

## Problem

Move four static menus (navbar create-new, navbar avatar (two variants), footer language, comment "...")
from Fomantic dropdowns to `<aria-menu>` with no visible change (AC5). Dropping `ui dropdown` from the
host loses four things Fomantic gave for free: (1) the `.ui.dropdown .menu` stylesheet, which
`aria-menu.css` only approximates (gap .5em vs .78rem, margin-top 4px vs 0, no min-height,
`.active`/`.selected`, header size, radius); (2) placement: right-aligned (`.left` auto-added on overflow
in the navbar), upward (footer), top-right pointing (comment); (3) `.active` on the open host (navbar
background, admin-badge border); (4) the `data-tooltip-content` to aria-label copy and tooltip
suppression for `jump` hosts. Constraints: keep `menu/item/header/divider` class names (issue Design
Decision); leave `dropdown.ts` alone; `#navbar .user-menu`, `.reference-issue[data-reference]`, item
classes and data attributes are read by JS and tests; tippy's `onShow` writes `aria-controls` on its
reference element.

## Usage (caller's view)

```html
<!-- web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md -->
<aria-menu placement="bottom-end" pointing>   <!-- placement: bottom-start (default) | bottom-end | top-start | top-end -->
  <button type="button" class="btn" data-tooltip-content="Create…">…</button>
  <div class="menu"><a class="item" href="…">…</a><div class="divider"></div>…</div>
</aria-menu>
```

Call sites: navbar `<aria-menu class="item" placement="bottom-end">`; footer
`<aria-menu placement="top-start">`; comment
`<aria-menu class="item action context-dropdown" placement="bottom-end" pointing>` with
`<button class="btn interact-fg context-menu" aria-label="More Operations">`. Full markup in
`sketch/templates.md`.

## Shape

- **Placement is a host attribute, read only by CSS.** `placement` uses the vocabulary of
  `data-tooltip-placement` (tippy/Floating UI), so one name already familiar in this repo covers all
  four corners with two selectors (`[placement^="top-"]`, `[placement$="-end"]`). `pointing` is a boolean
  attribute. `aria-menu.ts` gains one comment line and no code. The server already knows where each menu
  sits; for these menus Fomantic's runtime flip always produced the same answer. Per laziness-protocol.
- **Fomantic visuals are ported once into `aria-menu.css`**, making the file match its own header
  comment ("styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`"). Placement-independent rules from `dropdown.css` (item
  metrics, `.active`, `.selected`, `:active`, first/last radius, header size, host font-size and
  line-height) go here because any future consumer wants them. Rules that exist only because of where a
  menu sits stay with the stylesheet that owns that place: navbar box and mobile left-align in
  `navbar.css`, comment padding in `repo.css`, footer scroll height in `home.css`. No `:is()` grafts onto
  `dropdown.css`: those rules carry `!important` and Fomantic specificity, and would tie the component to
  a stylesheet #25 means to delete.
- **Open state comes from `aria-expanded`.** `#navbar .item:has(> [aria-expanded="true"])` joins the
  two existing `.item.active` selector lists. No `active` class mirrored onto the host, so the trigger's
  ARIA state is the only open/closed state.
- **The trigger is a real `<button type="button" class="btn">`**, the repo's existing chrome-free
  button reset, plus `interact-fg` for the kebab (same look as `a.muted`). The host keeps its layout
  classes (`item`, `item action`), so `.navbar-right > .item` (flex, mobile hiding) and
  `.comment-header-right > .item.action` keep matching. Padding moves from host to trigger so the whole
  pill is clickable. Because the trigger is not `.item`, `#navbar button.item:hover` adds no hover
  background the old menus never had.
- **Tooltip and name live on the trigger.** `attachLazyTooltip` then writes aria-label where AT reads it
  (the "+" button has no other name). One guard in `createTippy`'s onShow, keyed on
  `aria-haspopup="menu"` (set only by `<aria-menu>`; tippy menus use `"true"`): skip `aria-controls`
  (else it would point at the tooltip, not the menu), and refuse to show while `aria-expanded="true"`.
  Hiding on open needs no code: `hideOnClick` covers the mouse, and blur covers the keyboard.
- **Two selector fixes**: `common-page.ts` language handler, `showTemporaryTooltip`'s `closest()`.

Interface depth: callers learn two optional attributes. Positioning, styling parity, tooltip
interplay and keyboard behaviour stay hidden behind the element.

## Synthesis decision

*(arena fills this in)*

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept no overflow flip in exchange for zero measuring JS and screenshot-stable placement. A
  custom template that moves a menu must set `placement` itself.
- We accept small behaviour-neutral edits to the devtest page (menus lose their 4px offset, icon gap
  grows to .78rem), because the component's contract is parity with Fomantic.
- We accept a `:has()` dependency (already used in segment.css and markup CSS) in exchange for a single
  source of open state.
- We accept that the tippy guard treats "any `aria-haspopup=menu` element" as a menu button. Today only
  `<aria-menu>` sets that value.
- We accept copying Fomantic's per-type `:first-of-type` radius quirk, because exact parity is what AC5
  checks.

## Alternatives considered

- **Fomantic modifier classes on the host (`left`, `upward`, `pointing`) styled in aria-menu.css.**
  The surface is no smaller than the attributes. Readers would then see `upward` with no `ui dropdown`
  and assume Fomantic is involved. These words also collide with real Fomantic selectors (`.left.menu`,
  `.ui.pointing`).
- **JS auto-flip on open, as dropdown.ts:108 does.** Hides placement from callers but adds measuring on
  every open, a test surface, and layout flicker risk, to compute an answer the template already knows.
- **`:is(.ui.dropdown, aria-menu)` grafted into dropdown.css.** Smallest CSS diff, but it scatters the
  component's styling across a 900-line Fomantic file full of `!important`, and #25 cannot delete that
  file later.
- **Keep tooltip on host, add `aria-label` by hand on the trigger.** Two copies of one string, and the
  host still needs its own open-state tooltip suppression.

## Implementation reconciliation

*(empty until Phase D)*

## Open questions and risks

- Flex `align-items:center` vs Fomantic's block items could shift svg/text by about 1px. Is a
  pixel-diff threshold acceptable for AC5, or must the item go back to `display:block` (which breaks the
  devtest/#61 layout)?
- The footer language menu no longer flips left. Does "Português de Portugal" overflow at 360–480px?
  `.right-links {min-width:180px}` suggests the authors expected a left anchor, but verify on a phone
  viewport.
- Is "More Operations" (`repo.more_operations`) an acceptable name for the kebab, or does the team want
  a new locale key? (A new key needs translation work.)
- Custom CSS targeting `#navbar .ui.dropdown` breaks (the issue's open question). Add a release-note
  line.
- `tests/e2e/utils.ts` `clickDropdownItem` stays unused and untouched (AC6 is trivially met).

## Next implementation step

Port the CSS into `aria-menu.css` and convert the create-new menu first. Then diff it against
`.claude/verify-runs/issue-62-before/create-*.png`, since that menu exercises placement, the
trigger, the tooltip name and the open background.

<aria-menu placement="bottom-end" pointing>   <!-- placement: bottom-start (default) | bottom-end | top-start | top-end -->
  <button type="button" class="btn" data-tooltip-content="Create…">…</button>
  <div class="menu"><a class="item" href="…">…</a><div class="divider"></div>…</div>
</aria-menu>
```

Call sites: navbar `<aria-menu class="item" placement="bottom-end">`; footer
`<aria-menu placement="top-start">`; comment
`<aria-menu class="item action context-dropdown" placement="bottom-end" pointing>` with
`<button class="btn interact-fg context-menu" aria-label="More Operations">`. Full markup in
`sketch/templates.md`.

## Shape

- **Placement is a host attribute, read only by CSS.** `placement` uses the vocabulary of
  `data-tooltip-placement` (tippy/Floating UI), so one name already familiar in this repo covers all
  four corners with two selectors (`[placement^="top-"]`, `[placement$="-end"]`). `pointing` is a boolean
  attribute. `aria-menu.ts` gains one comment line and no code. The server already knows where each menu
  sits; for these menus Fomantic's runtime flip always produced the same answer. Per laziness-protocol.
- **Fomantic visuals are ported once into `aria-menu.css`**, making the file match its own header
  comment ("styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`"). Placement-independent rules from `dropdown.css` (item
  metrics, `.active`, `.selected`, `:active`, first/last radius, header size, host font-size and
  line-height) go here because any future consumer wants them. Rules that exist only because of where a
  menu sits stay with the stylesheet that owns that place: navbar box and mobile left-align in
  `navbar.css`, comment padding in `repo.css`, footer scroll height in `home.css`. No `:is()` grafts onto
  `dropdown.css`: those rules carry `!important` and Fomantic specificity, and would tie the component to
  a stylesheet #25 means to delete.
- **Open state comes from `aria-expanded`.** `#navbar .item:has(> [aria-expanded="true"])` joins the
  two existing `.item.active` selector lists. No `active` class mirrored onto the host, so the trigger's
  ARIA state is the only open/closed state.
- **The trigger is a real `<button type="button" class="btn">`**, the repo's existing chrome-free
  button reset, plus `interact-fg` for the kebab (same look as `a.muted`). The host keeps its layout
  classes (`item`, `item action`), so `.navbar-right > .item` (flex, mobile hiding) and
  `.comment-header-right > .item.action` keep matching. Padding moves from host to trigger so the whole
  pill is clickable. Because the trigger is not `.item`, `#navbar button.item:hover` adds no hover
  background the old menus never had.
- **Tooltip and name live on the trigger.** `attachLazyTooltip` then writes aria-label where AT reads it
  (the "+" button has no other name). One guard in `createTippy`'s onShow, keyed on
  `aria-haspopup="menu"` (set only by `<aria-menu>`; tippy menus use `"true"`): skip `aria-controls`
  (else it would point at the tooltip, not the menu), and refuse to show while `aria-expanded="true"`.
  Hiding on open needs no code: `hideOnClick` covers the mouse, and blur covers the keyboard.
- **Two selector fixes**: `common-page.ts` language handler, `showTemporaryTooltip`'s `closest()`.

Interface depth: callers learn two optional attributes. Positioning, styling parity, tooltip
interplay and keyboard behaviour stay hidden behind the element.

## Synthesis decision

*(arena fills this in)*

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept no overflow flip in exchange for zero measuring JS and screenshot-stable placement. A
  custom template that moves a menu must set `placement` itself.
- We accept small behaviour-neutral edits to the devtest page (menus lose their 4px offset, icon gap
  grows to .78rem), because the component's contract is parity with Fomantic.
- We accept a `:has()` dependency (already used in segment.css and markup CSS) in exchange for a single
  source of open state.
- We accept that the tippy guard treats "any `aria-haspopup=menu` element" as a menu button. Today only
  `<aria-menu>` sets that value.
- We accept copying Fomantic's per-type `:first-of-type` radius quirk, because exact parity is what AC5
  checks.

## Alternatives considered

- **Fomantic modifier classes on the host (`left`, `upward`, `pointing`) styled in aria-menu.css.**
  The surface is no smaller than the attributes. Readers would then see `upward` with no `ui dropdown`
  and assume Fomantic is involved. These words also collide with real Fomantic selectors (`.left.menu`,
  `.ui.pointing`).
- **JS auto-flip on open, as dropdown.ts:108 does.** Hides placement from callers but adds measuring on
  every open, a test surface, and layout flicker risk, to compute an answer the template already knows.
- **`:is(.ui.dropdown, aria-menu)` grafted into dropdown.css.** Smallest CSS diff, but it scatters the
  component's styling across a 900-line Fomantic file full of `!important`, and #25 cannot delete that
  file later.
- **Keep tooltip on host, add `aria-label` by hand on the trigger.** Two copies of one string, and the
  host still needs its own open-state tooltip suppression.

## Implementation reconciliation

*(empty until Phase D)*

## Open questions and risks

- Flex `align-items:center` vs Fomantic's block items could shift svg/text by about 1px. Is a
  pixel-diff threshold acceptable for AC5, or must the item go back to `display:block` (which breaks the
  devtest/#61 layout)?
- The footer language menu no longer flips left. Does "Português de Portugal" overflow at 360–480px?
  `.right-links {min-width:180px}` suggests the authors expected a left anchor, but verify on a phone
  viewport.
- Is "More Operations" (`repo.more_operations`) an acceptable name for the kebab, or does the team want
  a new locale key? (A new key needs translation work.)
- Custom CSS targeting `#navbar .ui.dropdown` breaks (the issue's open question). Add a release-note
  line.
- `tests/e2e/utils.ts` `clickDropdownItem` stays unused and untouched (AC6 is trivially met).

trigger, the tooltip name and the open background.

## Shape

**Variants are static host classes taken from Fomantic's own vocabulary and implemented generically in `aria-menu.css`:** `upward`, `right`, and the pair `right pointing`. Only the pair draws the arrow, so `pointing` used alone shows nothing. That way the incomplete form fails visibly instead of drawing a misplaced arrow (encode-lessons-in-structure). All four placements the before screenshots show are fixed by the design, not by the viewport. The navbar menus are right-aligned because they sit at the right edge, the kebab is right-aligned on purpose, and the footer always opens upward. A declarative class therefore reproduces them exactly, with no measuring, no layout reads on open, and deterministic screenshots. The one place where Fomantic's overflow flip did differ was the phone layout with `navbar-menu-open`, where hosts are full width and the menu opened left-aligned. One `#navbar aria-menu.right > .menu` reset inside navbar.css's existing `max-width: 767.98px` block covers it.

**The lost Fomantic rules go into generic `aria-menu.css`, copied value for value.** The file already claims to be "styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`". The design makes that claim true rather than adding a second per-menu layer. The ported rules are block items, the 2.57rem min-height, 1rem item font, svg `margin-right: .78rem` in place of flex `gap: .5em`, `.95em` headers, `.active`/`.selected`/`:active` backgrounds, the first/last-of-type radius quirk, popup margin 0 in place of 4px, and trigger `cursor`/`user-select`. Because these live in the shared file, every future migration inherits the Fomantic look for free (single source of truth).

**Per-menu CSS covers only the rules that were per-menu before.** Each such rule is rewritten in place where it already lives. `navbar.css`'s dead `#navbar .item.ui.dropdown {padding-right: 5px}` becomes "host padding 0, trigger takes `3px 5px 3px 13px` and stretches", so the whole pill stays clickable. The open-state shade becomes `#navbar aria-menu.item:has(> [aria-expanded="true"])`, derived from the attribute the component already owns instead of syncing an `active` class. `home.css` drops `.ui.dropdown` from the language-menu selector, which keeps the max-height, the scroll and the 10px bottom margin. `repo.css` moves the kebab's 4px padding from host to trigger, so the hit area stays at 24px.

**The trigger stays the existing `<span>`/`<a>`.** `aria-menu.ts` already makes a non-button trigger `role=button tabindex=0` and handles Enter, Space and the arrows on keydown. A `<button>` would add UA chrome to reset and drop the `a.muted` colour, with no gain for keyboard or assistive-technology users. The trigger CSS matches `aria-menu > :not(.menu)` rather than `[aria-haspopup]`, so nothing shifts in the window before init.

**The tooltip and accessible name move to the trigger.** `attachLazyTooltip` sets `aria-label` on whatever element carries `data-tooltip-content`. On the role-less host that label was ignored, which left the icon-only "+" button unnamed. On the trigger it names both the button and, through the existing `aria-labelledby`, the menu. The kebab gets a new `aria-label` from one new en-US key (`repo.issues.context.menu`), because it had no name before. The component's `open()` hides and disables `trigger._tippy`, and `close()` re-enables it. Those three lines go in the component because every icon trigger with a tooltip needs them, which makes this the deep-module placement.

**JS:** `common-page.ts` changes its selector to `.menu.language-menu`. `tippy.ts` changes to `closest('.ui.dropdown, aria-menu')`, which fixes the "Copied!" tooltip landing at 0,0. Every item handler is untouched. The dead `js-aria-clickable` comes off the kebab items, and the frontend-js doc and its guide twin are updated to match.

What the design deliberately does not do: no auto-flip JS, no `placement` attribute or property API, no `active` class syncing, no edits to `dropdown.ts` or `dropdown.css`, no change to `clickDropdownItem`.

Interface depth: the public surface grows by three CSS class names, all of which authors already know from Fomantic, plus one convention (tooltip on the trigger). The component's TS API does not change.

## Synthesis decision
## Shape

Answers to the central questions, each a position:

1. **Variants: host attributes, CSS-only** (`align="right"`, `direction="up"`, `pointing`). No JS auto-flip, no `:is()` reuse of Fomantic selectors (those are `.ui.dropdown`-scoped and dropdown.css is the file a later issue deletes; coupling to it defeats that cleanup). Class modifiers rejected: `left`/`right`/`top` collide with Fomantic/Tailwind generic names. `pointing` is defined only with `align="right"` (the sole use), so no unused arrow-left variant. Fomantic's overflow auto-flip is replaced by static choices matching where each menu sits; mobile navbar resets to left in one media query.
2. **Ported Fomantic rules go in aria-menu.css, generically**, not per menu. I change the component defaults to Fomantic's real values (block items, min-height, `svg` margin .78rem, margin 0, header .95em, first/last radius, `.active`/`.selected`/`:active`). The file already claims "styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`"; it was merely inexact. Cost: #61's devtest demo shifts by a few px (icon gap, 4px offset). Per-menu CSS would duplicate the same ~40 lines four times. Only genuinely site-specific rules stay local: navbar padding (navbar.css), comment padding (repo.css), language-menu scroll (home.css selector change).
3. **Trigger: keep the existing span/a**; the component already gives role=button + tabindex=0, and `[role=button]:focus-visible` already exists in base.css. A `<button>` would import UA chrome and `#navbar button.item:hover` surprises. Host padding moves to the trigger (`flex:1`, stretch) so the click area equals the old host. A one-rule `aria-menu > [role=button] {cursor; user-select}` replaces Fomantic's host rule.
4. **Accessible name and tooltip**: `data-tooltip-content` moves from host to trigger; `attachLazyTooltip` already derives `aria-label` there, so the name is on the role=button element (on the role-less host it was ignored by AT). The comment kebab gets an `aria-label` via one new locale key. **Tooltip hiding lives in the component** (`open()` hides+disables `trigger._tippy`; `close()` enables it after `focus()` so the restored focus doesn't re-show it). This replaces common-page.ts's `jump` handling for these menus and benefits every future aria-menu. (per laziness-protocol: no per-menu JS)
5. **Open-state styling**: component toggles `active` on the host in open/close. The existing `#navbar .item.active` rule works unchanged; `:has([aria-expanded])` rejected as it would need a second navbar selector and only works there.
6. JS selectors: common-page.ts `'aria-menu .menu.language-menu'`; tippy.ts `closest('.ui.dropdown, aria-menu')` so "Copied!" anchors to the visible host. Drop dead `js-aria-clickable` in context_menu.tmpl; fix frontend-js.md:103-108 + guide twin.

Interface depth: public surface grows by three attributes and zero methods; open state, tooltip suppression and ARIA stay hidden in the component. Invariant "the menu looks like Fomantic's" lives in one stylesheet.

43	## Gotchas
44	- Click target: host padding (3px 5px 3px 13px) sits outside the trigger; padding should move to trigger.
45	- A <button> trigger loses a.muted styling, gains UA chrome; `#navbar button.item:hover` may add hover bg navbar dropdowns never had.
46	- Mobile: with navbar-menu-open hosts are full-width and Fomantic opened left-aligned; a fixed right modifier would misplace on phones → scope to ≥768px.

51	## User Story
52	As a screen reader user, I want the menus I hit on every single page — the profile menu, the
53	create-new menu, the language menu and the comment "..." menu — to be the accessible ones, so
54	that the most-used menus in Gitea stop being the least usable ones.
55	
56	## User Scenario
57	A keyboard user Tabs along the top bar of the dashboard, reaches the avatar button, presses Enter,
58	arrows down to "Settings" and presses Enter. They scroll to the footer, Tab to the language menu,
59	open it the same way and pick a language. On an issue, they Tab to a comment's "..." button, open
60	it and choose "Copy link" — the same three keystrokes each time.
61	
62	## Acceptance Criteria
63	- [ ] AC1: Given the signed-in navbar, then the profile menu and the create-new menu in
64	      `templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl` use the component from #61 and no longer carry the
65	      `ui dropdown` class or get patched by `dropdown.ts`.
66	- [ ] AC2: Given the footer, then the language menu in `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` uses
67	      the component, and choosing a language still switches it — the click handler in
68	      `web_src/js/features/common-page.ts:27` still fires or is replaced by an equivalent.
69	- [ ] AC3: Given an issue comment, then the "..." menu in
70	      `templates/repo/issue/view_content/context_menu.tmpl` uses the component, and every item
71	      still works: copy link, copy source, quote reply, reference issue, edit and delete.
72	- [ ] AC4: Given each migrated menu, when opened with the keyboard, then all of AC1–AC6 of #61
73	      hold — arrows, Home/End, type-ahead, Escape-restores-focus and the ARIA attributes.
74	- [ ] AC5: Given each migrated menu, then its visual appearance on both the light and dark themes
75	      is unchanged from before the migration, verified by a before/after screenshot in the PR.
76	- [ ] AC6: Given the migrated menus, when the existing e2e suite runs, then it passes — including
77	      any test using `clickDropdownItem` from `tests/e2e/utils.ts` against a migrated menu, which
78	      must either keep working or be updated in this PR.
79	- [ ] AC7: Playwright tests cover keyboard operation of the profile menu and the comment "..."
80	      menu end to end.
81	
82	## Out of Scope
83	- The theme selector (`#footer-theme-selector`), whose menu is populated separately and is better
84	  migrated with the other JS-populated menus.
85	- Every dropdown that is a combobox, has a search input, or allows multiple selection — the issue
86	  sidebar label, assignee, reviewer, milestone and project menus all stay on Fomantic.
87	- The repository branch and tag selector.
88	- Deleting any part of `dropdown.ts`; it still serves the ~55 dropdowns left behind.
89	
90	## Open Questions
91	- Does anything outside the repo rely on the `.ui.dropdown` class on the navbar items for custom
92	  CSS? Gitea supports custom templates and stylesheets, so this may be a note-worthy change for
93	  the release notes.
94	
95	## Design Decision
96	**Decision:** Migrate only menus that are static, server-rendered and single-select, and keep the
97	existing Fomantic CSS class names on the new markup so the visual result is identical.
98	
99	**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Migrate every `ui dropdown` in `templates/` in one PR.
100	(b) Migrate the same three menus but also write fresh CSS for them instead of reusing the Fomantic
101	classes.
102	
103	**Rationale:** (a) is 61 occurrences spanning comboboxes, AJAX-populated lists and the label
104	multi-select — far past a sprint, and it would put untested changes on the issue sidebar, the most
105	complex dropdown in the product. The three chosen menus are the highest-traffic and the simplest,
106	so they give the most user benefit per unit of risk. On (b): reusing the class names keeps this PR
107	a behaviour change rather than a behaviour-plus-appearance change, which makes AC5 a screenshot
108	comparison instead of a design review, and keeps the diff reviewable.
109	
110	**Consequences:** Easier — a reviewer can check the diff against one criterion, "does it still
111	look and behave the same", and the remaining dropdowns are untouched so nothing else can regress.
112	Harder — the new component inherits Fomantic's CSS class names and therefore its stylesheet, so
113	Fomantic's CSS cannot be dropped even after every menu is migrated; that cleanup becomes a
114	separate, later issue and should be recorded as such in #25.
115	
116	## Scope
117	medium (5 points)

122	*Spec drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5) from `docs/sprint1/backlog-refinement.md`, posted by @Jack-Donohue.*
123	# #62 candidate c1: declarative placement, zero component JS
124	
125	Sketch files: `sketch/templates.md`, `sketch/css.md`, `sketch/ts.md`, `sketch/navbar-menus.test.ts`.
126	
127	## Problem
128	
129	Move four static menus (navbar create-new, navbar avatar (two variants), footer language, comment "...")
130	from Fomantic dropdowns to `<aria-menu>` with no visible change (AC5). Dropping `ui dropdown` from the
131	host loses four things Fomantic gave for free: (1) the `.ui.dropdown .menu` stylesheet, which
132	`aria-menu.css` only approximates (gap .5em vs .78rem, margin-top 4px vs 0, no min-height,
133	`.active`/`.selected`, header size, radius); (2) placement: right-aligned (`.left` auto-added on overflow
134	in the navbar), upward (footer), top-right pointing (comment); (3) `.active` on the open host (navbar
135	background, admin-badge border); (4) the `data-tooltip-content` to aria-label copy and tooltip
136	suppression for `jump` hosts. Constraints: keep `menu/item/header/divider` class names (issue Design
137	Decision); leave `dropdown.ts` alone; `#navbar .user-menu`, `.reference-issue[data-reference]`, item
138	classes and data attributes are read by JS and tests; tippy's `onShow` writes `aria-controls` on its
139	reference element.
140	
141	## Usage (caller's view)
142	
143	```html
144	<!-- web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md -->
145	<aria-menu placement="bottom-end" pointing>   <!-- placement: bottom-start (default) | bottom-end | top-start | top-end -->
146	  <button type="button" class="btn" data-tooltip-content="Create…">…</button>
147	  <div class="menu"><a class="item" href="…">…</a><div class="divider"></div>…</div>
148	</aria-menu>
149	```
150	
151	Call sites: navbar `<aria-menu class="item" placement="bottom-end">`; footer
152	`<aria-menu placement="top-start">`; comment
153	`<aria-menu class="item action context-dropdown" placement="bottom-end" pointing>` with
154	`<button class="btn interact-fg context-menu" aria-label="More Operations">`. Full markup in
155	`sketch/templates.md`.
156	
157	## Shape
158	
159	- **Placement is a host attribute, read only by CSS.** `placement` uses the vocabulary of
160	  `data-tooltip-placement` (tippy/Floating UI), so one name already familiar in this repo covers all
161	  four corners with two selectors (`[placement^="top-"]`, `[placement$="-end"]`). `pointing` is a boolean
162	  attribute. `aria-menu.ts` gains one comment line and no code. The server already knows where each menu
163	  sits; for these menus Fomantic's runtime flip always produced the same answer. Per laziness-protocol.
164	- **Fomantic visuals are ported once into `aria-menu.css`**, making the file match its own header
165	  comment ("styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`"). Placement-independent rules from `dropdown.css` (item
166	  metrics, `.active`, `.selected`, `:active`, first/last radius, header size, host font-size and
167	  line-height) go here because any future consumer wants them. Rules that exist only because of where a
168	  menu sits stay with the stylesheet that owns that place: navbar box and mobile left-align in
169	  `navbar.css`, comment padding in `repo.css`, footer scroll height in `home.css`. No `:is()` grafts onto
170	  `dropdown.css`: those rules carry `!important` and Fomantic specificity, and would tie the component to
171	  a stylesheet #25 means to delete.
172	- **Open state comes from `aria-expanded`.** `#navbar .item:has(> [aria-expanded="true"])` joins the
173	  two existing `.item.active` selector lists. No `active` class mirrored onto the host, so the trigger's
174	  ARIA state is the only open/closed state.
175	- **The trigger is a real `<button type="button" class="btn">`**, the repo's existing chrome-free
176	  button reset, plus `interact-fg` for the kebab (same look as `a.muted`). The host keeps its layout
177	  classes (`item`, `item action`), so `.navbar-right > .item` (flex, mobile hiding) and
178	  `.comment-header-right > .item.action` keep matching. Padding moves from host to trigger so the whole
179	  pill is clickable. Because the trigger is not `.item`, `#navbar button.item:hover` adds no hover
180	  background the old menus never had.
181	- **Tooltip and name live on the trigger.** `attachLazyTooltip` then writes aria-label where AT reads it
182	  (the "+" button has no other name). One guard in `createTippy`'s onShow, keyed on
183	  `aria-haspopup="menu"` (set only by `<aria-menu>`; tippy menus use `"true"`): skip `aria-controls`
184	  (else it would point at the tooltip, not the menu), and refuse to show while `aria-expanded="true"`.
185	  Hiding on open needs no code: `hideOnClick` covers the mouse, and blur covers the keyboard.
186	- **Two selector fixes**: `common-page.ts` language handler, `showTemporaryTooltip`'s `closest()`.
187	
188	Interface depth: callers learn two optional attributes. Positioning, styling parity, tooltip
189	interplay and keyboard behaviour stay hidden behind the element.
190	
191	## Synthesis decision
192	
193	*(arena fills this in)*
194	
195	## Tradeoffs accepted
196	
197	- We accept no overflow flip in exchange for zero measuring JS and screenshot-stable placement. A
198	  custom template that moves a menu must set `placement` itself.
199	- We accept small behaviour-neutral edits to the devtest page (menus lose their 4px offset, icon gap
200	  grows to .78rem), because the component's contract is parity with Fomantic.
201	- We accept a `:has()` dependency (already used in segment.css and markup CSS) in exchange for a single
202	  source of open state.
203	- We accept that the tippy guard treats "any `aria-haspopup=menu` element" as a menu button. Today only
204	  `<aria-menu>` sets that value.
205	- We accept copying Fomantic's per-type `:first-of-type` radius quirk, because exact parity is what AC5
206	  checks.
207	
208	## Alternatives considered
209	
210	- **Fomantic modifier classes on the host (`left`, `upward`, `pointing`) styled in aria-menu.css.**
211	  The surface is no smaller than the attributes. Readers would then see `upward` with no `ui dropdown`
212	  and assume Fomantic is involved. These words also collide with real Fomantic selectors (`.left.menu`,
213	  `.ui.pointing`).
214	- **JS auto-flip on open, as dropdown.ts:108 does.** Hides placement from callers but adds measuring on
215	  every open, a test surface, and layout flicker risk, to compute an answer the template already knows.
216	- **`:is(.ui.dropdown, aria-menu)` grafted into dropdown.css.** Smallest CSS diff, but it scatters the
217	  component's styling across a 900-line Fomantic file full of `!important`, and #25 cannot delete that
218	  file later.
219	- **Keep tooltip on host, add `aria-label` by hand on the trigger.** Two copies of one string, and the
220	  host still needs its own open-state tooltip suppression.
221	
222	## Implementation reconciliation
223	
224	*(empty until Phase D)*

245	# Candidate c2: static Fomantic-vocabulary host classes, zero placement JS
246	
247	Sketch files in this directory: `templates.sketch`, `aria-menu.css` (full proposed file), `css-callsites.diff`, `aria-menu.ts.sketch`, `js-selectors.diff`, `menus.test.ts.sketch`.
248	
249	## Problem
250	
251	Four menus move from `div.ui.dropdown` to `<aria-menu>`: navbar create-new, navbar profile (twice, counting the MustChangePassword variant), footer language, and the comment "..." menu. The visual target is the before set in `.claude/verify-runs/issue-62-before/`. In those screenshots both navbar menus open right-aligned with the host shaded, the language menu opens upward and left-aligned, and the comment menu opens right-aligned with an arrow at top right. Fomantic produces this through four mechanisms that disappear with the `ui dropdown` class: `dropdown.css` rules keyed on `.ui.dropdown`, a JS overflow check that adds `.left` (dropdown.ts:108-120), an `active` class on the open host, and tooltip code for `jump` hosts (common-page.ts:65-90). Constraints: the issue's Design Decision says to keep Fomantic class names and leave `dropdown.ts` alone. `features/repo-view-file-tree.ts` still queries `#navbar .user-menu`. The comment item handlers are delegated on `document` and key on the item classes and data attributes. Two JS call sites break: `common-page.ts:27` and `tippy.ts:190`. The only current consumer of `aria-menu.css` is the devtest page, so it can change freely.
252	
253	## Usage (caller's view)
254	
255	A template author writes Fomantic's markup with the host tag swapped and `ui dropdown` removed. Placement comes from the class names they already know:
256	
257	```html
258	<aria-menu class="item right">            <!-- navbar: right-aligned -->
259	  <span class="flex-text-block" data-tooltip-content="Create…">+ ▾</span>
260	  <div class="menu"><a class="item" href="/repo/create">…</a></div>
261	</aria-menu>
262	
263	<aria-menu class="upward">                 <!-- footer -->
264	  <span class="flex-text-inline">🌐 English</span>
265	  <div class="menu language-menu">…</div>
266	</aria-menu>
267	
268	<aria-menu class="item action right pointing context-dropdown">   <!-- comment kebab -->
269	  <a class="context-menu muted" aria-label="Comment actions">⋯</a>
270	  <div class="menu"><div class="item context" data-clipboard-text="…">Copy Link</div>…</div>
271	</aria-menu>
272	```
273	
274	The author's rule: the tooltip goes on the trigger, never on the host. Item JS stays unchanged except for one selector in `common-page.ts`.
275	
276	## Shape
277	
278	**Variants are static host classes taken from Fomantic's own vocabulary and implemented generically in `aria-menu.css`:** `upward`, `right`, and the pair `right pointing`. Only the pair draws the arrow, so `pointing` used alone shows nothing. That way the incomplete form fails visibly instead of drawing a misplaced arrow (encode-lessons-in-structure). All four placements the before screenshots show are fixed by the design, not by the viewport. The navbar menus are right-aligned because they sit at the right edge, the kebab is right-aligned on purpose, and the footer always opens upward. A declarative class therefore reproduces them exactly, with no measuring, no layout reads on open, and deterministic screenshots. The one place where Fomantic's overflow flip did differ was the phone layout with `navbar-menu-open`, where hosts are full width and the menu opened left-aligned. One `#navbar aria-menu.right > .menu` reset inside navbar.css's existing `max-width: 767.98px` block covers it.
279	
280	**The lost Fomantic rules go into generic `aria-menu.css`, copied value for value.** The file already claims to be "styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`". The design makes that claim true rather than adding a second per-menu layer. The ported rules are block items, the 2.57rem min-height, 1rem item font, svg `margin-right: .78rem` in place of flex `gap: .5em`, `.95em` headers, `.active`/`.selected`/`:active` backgrounds, the first/last-of-type radius quirk, popup margin 0 in place of 4px, and trigger `cursor`/`user-select`. Because these live in the shared file, every future migration inherits the Fomantic look for free (single source of truth).
281	
282	**Per-menu CSS covers only the rules that were per-menu before.** Each such rule is rewritten in place where it already lives. `navbar.css`'s dead `#navbar .item.ui.dropdown {padding-right: 5px}` becomes "host padding 0, trigger takes `3px 5px 3px 13px` and stretches", so the whole pill stays clickable. The open-state shade becomes `#navbar aria-menu.item:has(> [aria-expanded="true"])`, derived from the attribute the component already owns instead of syncing an `active` class. `home.css` drops `.ui.dropdown` from the language-menu selector, which keeps the max-height, the scroll and the 10px bottom margin. `repo.css` moves the kebab's 4px padding from host to trigger, so the hit area stays at 24px.
283	
284	**The trigger stays the existing `<span>`/`<a>`.** `aria-menu.ts` already makes a non-button trigger `role=button tabindex=0` and handles Enter, Space and the arrows on keydown. A `<button>` would add UA chrome to reset and drop the `a.muted` colour, with no gain for keyboard or assistive-technology users. The trigger CSS matches `aria-menu > :not(.menu)` rather than `[aria-haspopup]`, so nothing shifts in the window before init.
285	
286	**The tooltip and accessible name move to the trigger.** `attachLazyTooltip` sets `aria-label` on whatever element carries `data-tooltip-content`. On the role-less host that label was ignored, which left the icon-only "+" button unnamed. On the trigger it names both the button and, through the existing `aria-labelledby`, the menu. The kebab gets a new `aria-label` from one new en-US key (`repo.issues.context.menu`), because it had no name before. The component's `open()` hides and disables `trigger._tippy`, and `close()` re-enables it. Those three lines go in the component because every icon trigger with a tooltip needs them, which makes this the deep-module placement.
287	
288	**JS:** `common-page.ts` changes its selector to `.menu.language-menu`. `tippy.ts` changes to `closest('.ui.dropdown, aria-menu')`, which fixes the "Copied!" tooltip landing at 0,0. Every item handler is untouched. The dead `js-aria-clickable` comes off the kebab items, and the frontend-js doc and its guide twin are updated to match.
289	
290	What the design deliberately does not do: no auto-flip JS, no `placement` attribute or property API, no `active` class syncing, no edits to `dropdown.ts` or `dropdown.css`, no change to `clickDropdownItem`.
291	
292	Interface depth: the public surface grows by three CSS class names, all of which authors already know from Fomantic, plus one convention (tooltip on the trigger). The component's TS API does not change.
293	
294	## Synthesis decision
295	
296	(Filled in by arena.)
297	
298	## Tradeoffs accepted
299	
300	- We accept no viewport-overflow handling in exchange for deterministic, layout-read-free placement. A menu that can land anywhere would need a different solution, and none of these four can.
301	- We accept a phone-specific override in navbar.css in exchange for keeping `right` a pure, context-free class.
302	- We accept changing #61's devtest look (4px gap becomes 0, flex items become block) in exchange for `aria-menu.css` actually matching Fomantic, as its header comment says it does.
303	- We accept copying Fomantic's `:first-of-type` radius quirk, where the first `<a>` after a header gets top rounding, in exchange for pixel-identical hover states. A reader might take it for a bug, so a comment says why it's there.
304	- We accept `_tippy` knowledge inside the web component in exchange for not adding an event protocol between the component and tippy.ts.
305	
306	## Alternatives considered
307	
308	- **Port dropdown.ts's overflow flip into `aria-menu.ts` (auto-`left`).** Its surface is smaller (no classes), but it hides a layout read on every open and still cannot produce the kebab's right alignment or the footer's forced `upward`, since neither overflows. It would need the classes anyway, so it adds two mechanisms where one is enough.
309	- **Reuse Fomantic's rules via `:is(.ui.dropdown, aria-menu)` in dropdown.css.** This is the smallest CSS diff, but it ties `aria-menu` to roughly 900 lines of Fomantic selectors, so every rule edited for the 55 remaining dropdowns silently restyles the accessible ones. It also blocks the later Fomantic-CSS cleanup that the Design Decision already records as hard.
310	- **`placement="right-start"` attributes with a JS or CSS lookup.** This is a new vocabulary that contradicts the Design Decision's "keep Fomantic class names", for no capability these menus need.
311	
312	## Implementation reconciliation
313	
314	(Empty until Phase D.)
315

The 375px capture in the test plan answers this. If it does overflow, add `right` to that host inside a `max-width` rule in home.css. Do not add JS.

327	# Candidate c3: #62 menu migration, attributes + generic CSS, state in the component
328	
329	## Problem
330	
331	Move four static single-select menus (navbar profile x2 incl. MustChangePassword, create-new, footer language, comment "...") from Fomantic `.ui.dropdown` to `<aria-menu>` (#61), looking identical and keyboard-accessible. The component today only knows "popup below, left-aligned", and its CSS approximates `.ui.dropdown .menu` (flex+gap icons, 4px gap, no active/selected, no header size). Moving the host off `.ui.dropdown` silently drops: `active` on the host (navbar open bg), right/upward/pointing placement, the `jump` tippy suppression, the tooltip-to-aria-label copy, item/icon metrics, language-menu scroll CSS (home.css:94), and the `.ui.dropdown` selectors in common-page.ts:27 and tippy.ts:190. Constraints: keep Fomantic class names (menu/item/header/divider/active/selected) on the markup; do not touch dropdown.ts; only these menus; small diff.
332	
333	## Usage (caller's view)
334	
335	Template authors write markup only, variants are attributes on the host:
336	
337	```html
338	<aria-menu class="item" align="right">          <!-- navbar profile/create-new -->
339	<aria-menu direction="up">                       <!-- footer language -->
340	<aria-menu class="item action" align="right" pointing>  <!-- comment "..." -->
341	```
342	Trigger = the existing first child (span/a), data-tooltip-content and aria-label on it. No JS call sites change except two selectors. See `sketch/templates.html`.
343	
344	## Shape
345	
346	Answers to the central questions, each a position:
347	
348	1. **Variants: host attributes, CSS-only** (`align="right"`, `direction="up"`, `pointing`). No JS auto-flip, no `:is()` reuse of Fomantic selectors (those are `.ui.dropdown`-scoped and dropdown.css is the file a later issue deletes; coupling to it defeats that cleanup). Class modifiers rejected: `left`/`right`/`top` collide with Fomantic/Tailwind generic names. `pointing` is defined only with `align="right"` (the sole use), so no unused arrow-left variant. Fomantic's overflow auto-flip is replaced by static choices matching where each menu sits; mobile navbar resets to left in one media query.
349	2. **Ported Fomantic rules go in aria-menu.css, generically**, not per menu. I change the component defaults to Fomantic's real values (block items, min-height, `svg` margin .78rem, margin 0, header .95em, first/last radius, `.active`/`.selected`/`:active`). The file already claims "styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`"; it was merely inexact. Cost: #61's devtest demo shifts by a few px (icon gap, 4px offset). Per-menu CSS would duplicate the same ~40 lines four times. Only genuinely site-specific rules stay local: navbar padding (navbar.css), comment padding (repo.css), language-menu scroll (home.css selector change).
350	3. **Trigger: keep the existing span/a**; the component already gives role=button + tabindex=0, and `[role=button]:focus-visible` already exists in base.css. A `<button>` would import UA chrome and `#navbar button.item:hover` surprises. Host padding moves to the trigger (`flex:1`, stretch) so the click area equals the old host. A one-rule `aria-menu > [role=button] {cursor; user-select}` replaces Fomantic's host rule.
351	4. **Accessible name and tooltip**: `data-tooltip-content` moves from host to trigger; `attachLazyTooltip` already derives `aria-label` there, so the name is on the role=button element (on the role-less host it was ignored by AT). The comment kebab gets an `aria-label` via one new locale key. **Tooltip hiding lives in the component** (`open()` hides+disables `trigger._tippy`; `close()` enables it after `focus()` so the restored focus doesn't re-show it). This replaces common-page.ts's `jump` handling for these menus and benefits every future aria-menu. (per laziness-protocol: no per-menu JS)
352	5. **Open-state styling**: component toggles `active` on the host in open/close. The existing `#navbar .item.active` rule works unchanged; `:has([aria-expanded])` rejected as it would need a second navbar selector and only works there.
353	6. JS selectors: common-page.ts `'aria-menu .menu.language-menu'`; tippy.ts `closest('.ui.dropdown, aria-menu')` so "Copied!" anchors to the visible host. Drop dead `js-aria-clickable` in context_menu.tmpl; fix frontend-js.md:103-108 + guide twin.
354	
355	Interface depth: public surface grows by three attributes and zero methods; open state, tooltip suppression and ARIA stay hidden in the component. Invariant "the menu looks like Fomantic's" lives in one stylesheet.
356	
357	## Synthesis decision
358	
359	Single candidate; the arena orchestrator fills this in.
360	
361	## Tradeoffs accepted
362	
363	- We accept changing #61's component defaults (and its demo's look by a few px) in exchange for no duplicated per-menu CSS.
364	- We accept static alignment instead of overflow auto-flip in exchange for zero JS; the footer language menu stays left-aligned and could clip at very narrow widths (check 375px in screenshots; fix would be `align="right"` there).
365	- We accept duplicating ~40 lines of values from dropdown.css in exchange for dropdown.css becoming deletable later (the issue notes Fomantic CSS can't yet be dropped; this reduces that debt).
366	- Role-less span/a trigger instead of `<button>`: less semantic than native, but zero visual risk.
367	- `pointing` only with `align="right"`: looks like an incomplete feature, deliberately (YAGNI).
368	
369	## Alternatives considered
370	
371	- **Reuse Fomantic via `:is(.ui.dropdown, aria-menu)` rewrites in dropdown.css**: smallest new CSS but edits shared Fomantic remnants that serve ~55 dropdowns (regression risk the issue forbids) and entangles cleanup.
372	- **JS auto-flip/positioning (like dropdown.ts:108-120)**: handles overflow generally but adds ~30 lines of measurement code and mobile edge cases for four known placements. Hides more complexity, but unneeded here.
373	- **Per-menu CSS with the component untouched**: smallest component diff, largest total diff, and every future migration repeats it.
374	- **Native `<button>` triggers**: best semantics, needs a reset rule and risks navbar hover changes.
375	
376	## Implementation reconciliation
377	
378	Not started.
379	
380	## Open questions and risks
381	
382	- Do before/after screenshots at 1280 and 375px show footer language menu clipping? If so, should it be `align="right"`?
383	- Is shifting the #61 devtest demo (margin 0, icon spacing) acceptable to the #61 author?
384	- Sufficient locale: is adding an English-only key `repo.issues.context.menu` ("Comment actions") acceptable, vs reusing an existing string?
385	- Does `aria-menu.item` as flex child inside `.navbar-right` render the `.not-mobile` triangle spacing identically? Verify first.
386	- Release note for custom CSS relying on `.ui.dropdown` in navbar (issue open question).
387	
388	## Next implementation step
389	
390	Edit aria-menu.css to the Fomantic-exact values in `sketch/aria-menu.css.diff.css`, convert the navbar create-new menu, and screenshot it against `.claude/verify-runs/issue-62-before`.

import {isDocumentFragmentOrElementNode} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import type {Content, Instance, Placement, Props} from 'tippy.js';
import {html} from '../utils/html.ts';
import {stripTags} from '../utils.ts';

type TippyOpts = {
  role?: string,
  theme?: 'default' | 'tooltip' | 'menu' | 'box-with-header' | 'bare',
} & Partial<Props>;

const visibleInstances = new Set<Instance>();
const arrowSvg = html`<svg width="16" height="7"><path d="m0 7 8-7 8 7Z" class="tippy-svg-arrow-outer"/><path d="m0 8 8-7 8 7Z" class="tippy-svg-arrow-inner"/></svg>`;

export function createTippy(target: Element, opts: TippyOpts = {}): Instance {
  // the callback functions should be destructured from opts,
  // because we should use our own wrapper functions to handle them, do not let the user override them
  const {onHide, onShow, onDestroy, role, theme, arrow, ...other} = opts;

  const instance: Instance = tippy(target, {
    appendTo: document.body,
    animation: false,
    allowHTML: false,
    hideOnClick: false,
    interactiveBorder: 20,
    ignoreAttributes: true,
    maxWidth: 500, // increase over default 350px
    onHide: (instance: Instance) => {
      visibleInstances.delete(instance);
      return onHide?.(instance);
    },
    onDestroy: (instance: Instance) => {
      visibleInstances.delete(instance);
      return onDestroy?.(instance);
    },
    onShow: (instance: Instance) => {
      // hide other tooltip instances so only one tooltip shows at a time
      for (const visibleInstance of visibleInstances) {
        if (visibleInstance.props.role === 'tooltip') {
          visibleInstance.hide();
        }
      }
      visibleInstances.add(instance);
      target.setAttribute('aria-controls', instance.popper.id);
      return onShow?.(instance);
    },
    arrow: arrow ?? (theme === 'bare' ? false : arrowSvg),
    // HTML role attribute, ideally the default role would be "popover" but it does not exist
    role: role || 'menu',
    // CSS theme, either "default", "tooltip", "menu", "box-with-header" or "bare"
    theme: theme || role || 'default',
    offset: [0, arrow ? 10 : 6],
    plugins: [followCursor],
    ...other,
  } satisfies Partial<Props>);

  if (instance.props.role === 'menu') {
    target.setAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'true');
  }

  return instance;
}

 * If the target element already has a tooltip tippy attached, the tooltip will be updated with the new content.
 * If the target element has no content, then no tooltip will be attached, and it returns null.
 *
 * Note: "tooltip" doesn't equal to "tippy". "tooltip" means a auto-popup content, it just uses tippy as the implementation.
 */
function attachTooltip(target: Element, content: Content | null = null): Instance | null {

  if (!target._tippy) {

  } else {

import {generateElemId, hideElem, showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// A menu button following https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/ with no Fomantic.
// Markup: <aria-menu><button type="button">label</button><div class="menu"><a class="item">...</a></div></aria-menu>
// Items get real focus (roving tabindex) instead of aria-activedescendant, see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md
window.customElements.define('aria-menu', class extends HTMLElement {
  trigger!: HTMLElement;
  popup!: HTMLElement;
  inited = false;

  connectedCallback() {
    // in <head>-loaded components, the children are not parsed yet while the page is still loading
    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init, {once: true});
    } else {
      this.init();
    }
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    document.removeEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init);
    if (this.inited) this.close(false); // also removes the outside click listener
  }

  init = () => {
    if (this.inited) return;
    const popup = this.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .menu');
    const trigger = Array.from(this.children).find((el) => el !== popup) as HTMLElement | undefined;
    if (!popup || !trigger) return;
    this.inited = true;
    this.popup = popup;
    this.trigger = trigger;

    if (trigger.tagName !== 'BUTTON') {
      trigger.setAttribute('role', 'button');
      trigger.tabIndex = 0;
    }
    if (!popup.id) popup.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-popup-');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-controls', popup.id);
    popup.setAttribute('role', 'menu');
    if (!popup.hasAttribute('aria-label') && !popup.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby')) {
      if (!trigger.id) trigger.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-trigger-');
      popup.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', trigger.id); // keeps the menu's name once focus is on an item
    }
    hideElem(popup);
    this.updateItemRoles();

    trigger.addEventListener('click', () => this.isOpen() ? this.close(true) : this.open('first'));
    trigger.addEventListener('keydown', this.onTriggerKeyDown);
    trigger.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('keydown', this.onPopupKeyDown);
    popup.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
      // bubble phase, so the item's own click handlers have already run
      if ((e.target as Element).closest('[role="menuitem"]')) this.close(true);
    });
  };

  // items may be added after init, e.g. by a feature script, so refresh them on every open
  updateItemRoles() {
    for (const child of this.popup.children) {
      if (child.classList.contains('item')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem');
        child.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      } else if (child.classList.contains('divider')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'separator');
      } else {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'none');
      }
    }
  }

  items(): HTMLElement[] {
    // hidden items can't take focus, so leaving them in would stall opening and arrow keys
    return Array.from(this.popup.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(':scope > [role="menuitem"]:not(.tw-hidden)'));
  }

  isOpen() {
    return this.trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
  }

  open(focus: 'first' | 'last') {
    this.updateItemRoles();
    showElem(this.popup);
    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    const items = this.items();
    (focus === 'first' ? items[0] : items.at(-1))?.focus();
  }

  close(restoreFocus: boolean) {
    // only restore when focus is still in the popup, so focus moved elsewhere by an item handler is kept
    const focusInPopup = this.popup.contains(document.activeElement);
    hideElem(this.popup);
    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    if (restoreFocus && focusInPopup) this.trigger.focus();
  }

  onPointerDownOutside = (e: Event) => {
    if (!this.contains(e.target as Node)) this.close(false);
  };

  // a native button fires "click" on Space keyup, which would toggle the menu shut again or double-activate an item
  preventSpaceClick = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault();
  };

  onTriggerKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      this.open('first');
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      this.open('last');
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();

# CSS sketches (c1)

Split: anything a second `<aria-menu>` consumer would also want goes in `aria-menu.css` (the file's
own header already promises "styled to match `.ui.dropdown .menu`"); anything that only exists
because of where a menu sits (navbar box, comment header padding, footer scroll height) goes in the
stylesheet that already owns that place. No `:is(.ui.dropdown, aria-menu)` edits in dropdown.css.

## web_src/css/modules/aria-menu.css (full file after the change)

```css
/* the <aria-menu> web component, styled to match ".ui.dropdown .menu" so migrated menus look the same */
aria-menu {
  display: inline-block;
  position: relative;
  font-size: 1rem;                           /* new: ".ui.dropdown" host metrics, the em-based arrow and offsets depend on it */
  line-height: var(--line-height-default);   /* new */
}

/* a .btn trigger replaces a span, keep the host's text metrics (normalize.css sets 1.15) */
aria-menu > .btn {
  line-height: inherit;
}

aria-menu > .menu {
  position: absolute;
  top: 100%;
  left: 0;
  z-index: 11;
  min-width: max-content;
  margin: 0;                                 /* was margin-top: 4px; Fomantic uses 0 */
  padding: 0;
  background: var(--color-menu);
  color: var(--color-text);
  border: 1px solid var(--color-secondary);
  border-radius: var(--border-radius);
  box-shadow: 0 6px 18px var(--color-shadow);
  text-align: left;
}

/* placement="(bottom|top)-(start|end)" mirrors data-tooltip-placement; the server knows where each menu sits */
aria-menu[placement$="-end"] > .menu {
  left: auto;
  right: 0;
}

aria-menu[placement^="top-"] > .menu {
  top: auto;
  bottom: 100%;
  border-radius: var(--border-radius) var(--border-radius) 0 0;
}

/* "pointing" is only drawn for bottom placements */
aria-menu[pointing] > .menu {
  margin-top: 1em;
}

aria-menu[pointing] > .menu::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: -0.25em;
  left: 1em;
  width: 0.5em;
  height: 0.5em;
  transform: rotate(45deg);
  background: var(--color-menu);
  box-shadow: -1px -1px 0 0 var(--color-secondary);
  z-index: 2;
  pointer-events: none;
}

aria-menu[pointing][placement$="-end"] > .menu::after {
  left: auto;
  right: 1em;
}

/* the element upgrades in <head> but only sets up its children at DOMContentLoaded, keep the popup hidden until then */
aria-menu > .menu:not([role="menu"]) {
  display: none;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.78rem;                              /* was 0.5em; Fomantic's svg margin-right */
  min-height: 2.57142857rem;                 /* new */
  padding: 0.78571429rem 1.14285714rem;
  font-size: 1rem;                           /* new */
  color: var(--color-text);
  line-height: var(--line-height-default);
  white-space: nowrap;
  cursor: pointer;
  text-decoration: none;
}

/* same quirk as Fomantic: per element type, so the first <a> after a <div class="header"> is rounded too */
aria-menu > .menu > .item:first-of-type {
  border-radius: var(--border-radius) var(--border-radius) 0 0;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item:last-of-type {
  border-radius: 0 0 var(--border-radius) var(--border-radius);
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item.selected,
aria-menu > .menu > .item:hover,
aria-menu > .menu > .item:focus {
  background: var(--color-hover);
  outline: none;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item.active,
aria-menu > .menu > .item:active {
  background: var(--color-active);
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary);
  outline-offset: -2px;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .divider {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--color-secondary);
  margin: 4px 0;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .header {
  margin: 1rem 0 0.75rem;
  padding: 0 1.14285714rem;
  font-size: 0.95em;                         /* new */
  font-weight: var(--font-weight-medium);
}
```

Ordering note: `.active` after `:hover/:focus` so the current page's item (Settings, Site
Administration) keeps `--color-active` while hovered, which is what Fomantic did (its `.active.item`
rule has higher specificity than `:hover`). The `.user-menu > .item {border-radius: 0 !important}` in
base.css still overrides the first/last radius on the avatar menu, exactly as before.

## web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts — createTippy's onShow wrapper

The tooltip moves from the roleless host to the trigger (so `attachLazyTooltip`'s aria-label lands on
an element AT reads). Two facts then bite: tippy's `onShow` overwrites `aria-controls` (which
`<aria-menu>` set to the popup id), and the tooltip can show over the open menu on re-hover. One guard
fixes both, keyed on attributes `<aria-menu>` already sets. tippy's own menus set
`aria-haspopup="true"`, so they are unaffected.

```ts
onShow: (instance: Instance) => {
  const isMenuButton = target.getAttribute('aria-haspopup') === 'menu'; // an <aria-menu> trigger
  if (isMenuButton && target.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') return false; // don't cover the open menu
  // hide other tooltip instances so only one tooltip shows at a time
  for (const visibleInstance of visibleInstances) { /* unchanged */ }
  visibleInstances.add(instance);
  if (!isMenuButton) target.setAttribute('aria-controls', instance.popper.id); // keep pointing at the menu
  return onShow?.(instance);
},
```

Why no explicit hide on open: mouse open = click, and tooltips use `hideOnClick: true`; keyboard
open moves focus into the menu, and tippy's `focus` trigger hides on blur. The guard covers the rest
(pointer re-entering the trigger while open). Replaces what `common-page.ts` did for `jump` hosts.

/* PROPOSED full replacement of web_src/css/modules/aria-menu.css.

/* the <aria-menu> web component, styled to match ".ui.dropdown .menu" so migrated menus look the same */
aria-menu {
  display: inline-block;
  position: relative;
}

/* the trigger, matched statically so nothing shifts before init sets aria-haspopup */
aria-menu > :not(.menu) {
  cursor: pointer;
  user-select: none;
}

aria-menu > .menu {
  position: absolute;
  top: 100%;
  left: 0;
  z-index: 11;
  min-width: max-content;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  background: var(--color-menu);
  color: var(--color-text);
  border: 1px solid var(--color-secondary);
  border-radius: var(--border-radius);
  box-shadow: 0 6px 18px var(--color-shadow);
  text-align: left;
  cursor: auto;
}

/* the element upgrades in <head> but only sets up its children at DOMContentLoaded, keep the popup hidden until then */
aria-menu > .menu:not([role="menu"]) {
  display: none;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item {
  display: block;
  min-height: 2.57142857rem;
  padding: 0.78571429rem 1.14285714rem;
  font-size: 1rem;
  color: var(--color-text);
  line-height: var(--line-height-default);
  white-space: nowrap;
  cursor: pointer;
  text-decoration: none;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item > svg {
  margin-right: 0.78rem;
}

/* Fomantic matches by tag, so after a .header the first <a> still gets the top radius; kept for identical hover shapes */
aria-menu > .menu > .item:first-of-type {
  border-radius: var(--border-radius) var(--border-radius) 0 0;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item:last-of-type {
  border-radius: 0 0 var(--border-radius) var(--border-radius);
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item:hover,
aria-menu > .menu > .item:focus,
aria-menu > .menu > .item.selected {
  background: var(--color-hover);
  outline: none;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item.active,
aria-menu > .menu > .item:active {
  background: var(--color-active);
}

aria-menu > .menu > .item:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary);
  outline-offset: -2px;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .divider {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--color-secondary);
  height: 0;
  margin: 4px 0;
}

aria-menu > .menu > .header {
  margin: 1rem 0 0.75rem;
  padding: 0 1.14285714rem;
  font-size: 0.95em;
  font-weight: var(--font-weight-medium);
}

/* placement modifiers use Fomantic's own host class names, so the template diff is "drop ui dropdown" */
aria-menu.upward > .menu {
  top: auto;
  bottom: 100%;
  border-radius: var(--border-radius) var(--border-radius) 0 0;
}

aria-menu.right > .menu {
  left: auto;
  right: 0;
}

/* only the combination is defined: "pointing" alone draws nothing rather than a misplaced arrow */
aria-menu.right.pointing > .menu {

aria-menu.right.pointing > .menu::after {

// Markup: <aria-menu><button type="button">label</button><div class="menu"><a class="item">...</a></div></aria-menu>
// Optional host attributes, CSS only: placement="bottom-end|top-start|top-end" (default bottom-start), pointing

```

The attribute vocabulary as a type, for the reader only (not added to the codebase, nothing consumes it):

type AriaMenuPlacement = 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'top-start' | 'top-end';
type AriaMenuHostAttrs = {placement?: AriaMenuPlacement; pointing?: ''};

## web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts — createTippy's onShow wrapper

The tooltip moves from the roleless host to the trigger (so `attachLazyTooltip`'s aria-label lands on
an element AT reads). Two facts then bite: tippy's `onShow` overwrites `aria-controls` (which
`<aria-menu>` set to the popup id), and the tooltip can show over the open menu on re-hover. One guard
fixes both, keyed on attributes `<aria-menu>` already sets. tippy's own menus set
`aria-haspopup="true"`, so they are unaffected.

```ts
onShow: (instance: Instance) => {
  const isMenuButton = target.getAttribute('aria-haspopup') === 'menu'; // an <aria-menu> trigger
  if (isMenuButton && target.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') return false; // don't cover the open menu
  // hide other tooltip instances so only one tooltip shows at a time
  for (const visibleInstance of visibleInstances) { /* unchanged */ }
  visibleInstances.add(instance);
  if (!isMenuButton) target.setAttribute('aria-controls', instance.popper.id); // keep pointing at the menu
  return onShow?.(instance);
},
```

Why no explicit hide on open: mouse open = click, and tooltips use `hideOnClick: true`; keyboard
open moves focus into the menu, and tippy's `focus` trigger hides on blur. The guard covers the rest
(pointer re-entering the trigger while open). Replaces what `common-page.ts` did for `jump` hosts.
